End of the road for Singh and Koko

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
This week former Eskom CEO Anoj Singh and head of Generation Matshela Koko testified at the state capture inquiry

Unique Selling Point:
We have an Eskom whistleblower and we have a former finance minister grilling the men at the heart of Eskom's state capture

Summary:
Eskom has one week left. If it doesnt release its financials the JSE will suspend its bonds. It also needs to urgently find R20 billion rand to keep going. Finance Minister Malusi Gigaba says treasury is not going to bail it out. Yet if Eskom gets a default letter from the World bank, a very likely possibility, it will trigger a run on its debt as the banks call in their loans. If that happens it could trigger a cross default across all state owned enterprises and bring the South African economy to its knees.

Further information:
South Africans weary of corruption and looting on a grand scale waited in anticipation for the Parliamentary testimonies of former Eskom CFO Anoj Singh and executive Matshela Koko who has spent the bulk of his career at Eskom. But if they were looking for an admission from Singh it wasnt coming. He denied, he deflected and he couldnt recall, and even in the face of a humiliating grilling from advocate Vanara he still maintained he had done a great job at Eskom. Singh seemed to age visibly during his almost 12 hour grilling, and one had to stay up late to watch the coup de Grace, delivered by former Finance minister Pravin Gordhan. On Wednesday Suzanne Daniels Eskom head of legal and compliance will take to her seat to watch Matshela Koko who has shifted some of the blame onto her shoulders. We capture her comments as his testimony unfolds.

Press Release:


Eskom: Deflections and Denials
It’s been a busy few days for Eskom, from the announcement of the new Board to the resignation of former CFO Anoj Singh. This week Singh and Head of Generation, Matshela Koko, also appeared before parliament's inquiry into the power utility, but if MPs were hoping for straight answers they were bitterly disappointed. Instead, Singh and Koko denied, deflected or simply couldn’t recall their roles in the events which some MPs say, brought Eskom to its knees. Carte Blanche unpacks this developing story.


Script:


FINAL SCRIPT DENIALS AND DEFLECTIONS/ End of the road KOKO/ SINGH Sunday 28th Jan

Commentary One
This week Suzanne Daniels spent long hours in front of her TV. Like many South Africans she stayed up late to watch the testimony in parliament of two of Eskom's top executives- Matshela Koko and Anoj Singh

Suzanne
Ooohhh….

Commentary Two
These men were her Eskom colleagues at Eskom. She considered Matshela Koko a friend, but that all ended last year when, as the head of legal and compliance, she blew the whistle on Eskom's secrets. Now at home on suspension herself, Suzanne spent Tuesday watching Singh's eleven- hour grilling

Up Sound TV Pravin
You are literally taking us for fools

Suzanne
I was a bit disappointed - you know the: "I don't know, I can't remember I wasn't there." I thought he would take the opportunity to come clean

Commentary Three
This committee of opposing parties probing graft into Eskom, Transnet and Denel has formed a united front against corruption under the leadership of Ntuthuzelo Vanara and the chair Zukiswa Rantho. They work long hours, take no prisoners, and South African's love them

Zukiswe Rantho
Throughout this process we have been subjected to all forms of intimidation, insults and even threats to ourselves and our families, we have stood our ground and defended the principles that our constitutional democracy was founded on.

Commentary Four
This is the Optimum mine that feeds Hendrina power station. In April 2016 in a late- night meeting of Eskom executives, they conspired to prepay the Gupta linked Tegeta R600 million rand for coal, even though Tegeta didn't yet own the mine. That R600 million helped the Gupta's buy the mine, and Eskom allegedly manufactured a coal emergency to justify pushing through the deal quickly

Suzanne
I think the emergency had been created so it was pretty much drafting as we went along...I now understand why they needed the time frame because there was a payment due the next day



Commentary Five
In just under three years the Gupta's and their associated companies that include Duduzane Zuma have made billions out of their coal mines. They have supplied substandard coal, placed power stations at risk, but still Eskom looked after them. And its these deals, including the prepayment to Tegeta that interested the committee

Vanara
I put it to you Mr Singh the reason you can't answer this question is you were bending backwards and forth, almost breaking your back to accommodate only one company Tegeta?

Singh
That is rather harsh summary, I don't think I was bending over in any way shape or form. I was presented with a transaction that needed to be executed with a mandate from the shareholder

Commentary six
On Monday after 2.5 years in the job, Singh who was the CFO resigned.

Suzanne
His work ethic was phenomenal, he would be in the office early -the detail he would read, and give you guidance and feedback. The man I saw yesterday was not the person that we worked with

Commentary Seven
If attention to detail was his thing, it was odd then, when the facts were inconvenient, that he couldn't remember ever seeing an email included in his own submission that discussed PFMA requirements on the McKinsey deal.

Vanara
For you to have quoted in your submission you must have had that email in front of you or did you miraculously know about the contents of an email that you have never seen before
Singh
No Sir
Vanara
I put it to you that your conduct was a deliberate ploy on your part to distort the advice you received and secondly to mislead the committee
Singh
I deny that categorically Sir. This is the first time I see this email

Suzanne:
I think there was a lot that he wasn't telling the committee

LINK
Dubai! Dubai! Everyone was in Dubai and the email trail, despite denials shows the payments for the hotels, led back to the Gupta family
Vanara
I am going to show you an invoice that relates to your travels in Dubai. To whom is it addressed?
Singh
Sahara computers
Vanara
Why would that invoice be directed to SAHARA computers?
Singh
I am not aware. I don't know

Commentary eight
As the hot afternoon wore on Pravin Gordhan's patience wore thin.

Pravin
You think we are little children, that each time we ask you a question you say I don't remember, its somebody else that did it, I am not responsible

Commentary nine
Singh told the committee he was proud of his work at Eskom, but under his watch as the CFO, Eskom is effectively bankrupt and its put the entire country's economy at risk

Suzanne Daniels
We are on the brink of financial ruin. I was at pains to figure out what was he proud of.
We have bankers not wanting to give us money, we haven't released our financial results that has never happened at Eskom before

LINK
Governance or the absence of it, was a key focus of the committee, and the former finance
Minister Minister bore down on Singh for his lack of accountability as the CFO

Commentary ten
Singh, said Gordhan had breached the companies act and the PFMA

Pravin
You aware that you are a delinquent director
Singh
I dispute I am a delinquent director
Pravin
Oh Okay

Commentary eleven
Last year at the Eskom results presentation Singh admitted to journalists that he had signed a R1.6 billion rand guarantee in favour of Tegeta. 6 months earlier Eskom had asked treasury for a R23 Billion- rand bailout. And that proved convenient when Tegeta needed money to buy Optimum. Gordhan was fuming


Pravin
Did you inform treasury about the guarantee?
Anoj Singh
No sir
Pravin
Ok so that is a clean violation there as well! If one actually puts this picture together, it's a huge conspiracy to ensure that Oakbay gets access to this business, and all of you in the top management were part of this conspiracy? And now you are going to say no
Anoj Singh
I agree we would say no
Pravin
We would expect that of you, and the public out there expects that of you too

Suzanne Daniels
He was echoing the feelings of 50 million South Africans and if Anoj didn't realise it at that point, then it is lost on him

Singh
Sir as I said to you before if there was accountability, I would take it
Pravin
Of-course you must take accountability! There have been downgrades on your watch! There is a liquidity problem on your watch! You have been part of bringing Eskom down to its knees …the biggest utility on the African continent

LINK
Matshela Koko didn't watch this humiliating scolding of his colleague. Instead he went to bed early knowing that he would have to face the music the next day.

Commentary twelve
Unlike Singh, Matshela Koko, an engineer, has made his career at Eskom for the last 23 years. As head of generation he manages a budget of billions.

Up Sound Koko
For those who know me I always say my blood is Eskom blue.

Commentary thirteen
But what could have been a brilliant career has now been marred by several scandals and allegations of his association with the Gupta's. In 2016, we confronted Mr Koko about the Gupta coal contracts

Devi
Are you sick and tired of answering questions about the Gupta's, these people seem to be a headache in terms of your business?
Koko
I am sick and tired of people wanting us to treat them differently, because they are not different because the assumption is that they cannot put an honest tender and win it.

Commentary fourteen
But an honest tender and the Gupta's don't sit comfortably in the same sentence.
The state capture report, the Gupta leaks and this inquiry paint a damning picture, and unfortunately for Mr Koko, Suzanne Daniels and others have spilled the beans on his association with Salim Essa - the man at the heart of the Gupta Empire

Suzanne
You were quite good friends with KOKO, it must be very difficult to have got to this point?
Suzanne
Yes it is- I think you can hear the trembling in my voice, when I realized the extent to which he was actually culpable, it was quite devastating

Commentary fifteen
Like Singh, Koko has also been to Dubai, but he denies that the Gupta's or companies associated with them paid for the trip. DA MP Natasha Mazzone was also interested in e mails that linked him to Tony Gupta before signing the Optimum deal.

Natasha
An email left Matshela2010.com and it went to the DG of public enterprises. And it said please give to the boss the fight begins and that email was then forwarded to Rajesh Gupta otherwise known as Tony Gupta. Who are we calling the boss and what fight is on?
Koko
I have never sent an email to DG David Seleke. Never done that

LINK
In June 2016 when I confronted Mr. Koko on why he had agreed for Eskom to prepay Tegeta R600 million and he said he had made a mistake.

Devi
So did you prepay?

Devi….
But Mr Koko you said no …
No no
But when I asked you said no?
Koko
Ok lets say I made a mistake lets do that

LINK
Now two years later, he had an explanation for that 'mistake'

Commentary sixteen
Koko argues that we should have asked him if Eskom prepaid Tegeta, the company that owns Optimum

Koko
The actual interview was asked was did Eskom prepay Optimum. I said no

Commentary seventeen
He is correct, but even at Eskom they use the term interchangeably, and he didn't see fit to correct us at the time. Perhaps because I also asked him if he prepaid Tegeta. Listen carefully Mr. Koko

Up sound Devi Carte Blanche
According to this Tegeta has requested some form of prepayment, so what is this?
Koko
You see all the cost- plus mines are prepayment and that is not surprise for me

Commentary eighteen
But Mr Koko has far bigger problems than Carte Blanche. Last weekend, along with Anoj Singh he was singled out by government for removal. On Thursday he was given an ultimatum by Eskom to resign or be fired, But Koko is defiant and asked the labour court to intervene. So, on Monday he's back to work

THE END 12 00

PROMO ONE 10 seconds
This was the week of denials as Eskom's Anoj Singh and Matshela Koko, head of generation faced a grilling by MP'S in parliament

PROMO TWO
This week Eskom former CFO Anoj Singh gets a humiliating dressing down by former finance minister Pravin Gordhan
Singh
Sir as I said to you before if there was accountability, I would take it
Pravin
Of-course you must take accountability! There have been downgrades on your watch!

PROMO THREE
Head of Eskom's generation Matshela Koko, maintains his innocence in parliament and faces a storm at work

Up Sound Koko
For those who know me I always say my blood is Eskom blue.
